paragraphs.text: Here is the thesis of the whole passage: beauty is not decoration, it is the cause. The groves do not just happen to be pretty while love happens nearby. They shine specifically for love’s sake — the other way round from what you would expect. The grove is what sets the mood off; the dust of passion gets so thick it blots out the sun and the moon; peacocks drunk on new clouds cry out.

The details are not ornaments either, they are responses to the mood. The kuTaja tree gets mocked by showy flowers, and the poet sides with the humble tree. The nIpa tree lets its body go to the bees — a release. The bee kisses the yUthikA creeper. The point of all of it is aesthetic: the feeling itself is what everything is for.
